chunks: We have seen you turn your face to the heavens. We shall turn you to a Qiblah that will please you. So turn towards the Holy Mosque, and turn towards it wherever you be. And those who are recipients of the Book surely know that this is the truth from their Lord; and God is not negligent of all that you do.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْكِتَابِ: People of the Book (Jews and Christians)
key_terms.أَوَّلُ الصَّلَاةِ: the first prayer (implied context of the change)
key_terms.تَقَلُّبَ وَجْكَ: turning of your face (looking towards the sky in anticipation)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the change of Qiblah in Islam and who recognizes it as truth?
ai.summary: This pivotal verse (2:144) marks the historical transition of the Qiblah from Jerusalem to the Kaaba, symbolizing the distinct identity of the Muslim Ummah and the completion of divine guidance. Shia scholarship highlights this shift as a test of faith and a confirmation that the People of the Book recognize the truth, while emphasizing God's omniscience over all ritual actions.
